text:
The bug is in `toolz/dicttoolz.py`, within `dissoc`.

When fewer than 60% of the dictionary’s keys are requested for removal, `dissoc` copies the input and executes `del d2[key]` for each requested key. A missing key therefore raises `KeyError`. The alternate branch uses set difference and already ignores missing keys, explaining the size-dependent behavior.

I will change the removal loop to delete only keys present in the copied dictionary (for example, by using `d2.pop(key, None)`), preserving the copied-result and input-immutability behavior.
